consumers.note: all four external callers pass the same holder +0x1240 field as the root argument; the routine is reached only by code, never by a stored reference

sites.role: self-recursive call extending the +0x18 descent past the unrolled depth

node_layout.down_link: +0x18: first child; the subtree rooted here is destroyed before the node itself
node_layout.next_link: +0x10: next sibling; followed after the node itself is destroyed
node_layout.payload: +0x30: refcounted pointer released through 0x5d350c0 when non-null

order: release [node +0x30] through 0x5d350c0 when non-null, skipped when null
sized delete of the node itself with size 0x38 via _ZdlPvm, unconditional
per_node_teardown.release_helper_contract: the shared refcount release established in the RE-001 three-release packet: null-skipped by the caller, not by the helper

arguments.rdi: root node of the structure to destroy; null returns immediately with nothing destroyed

routine.frame_note: FDE carries cie=00000000, so no landing pads; no stack canary

traversal.assumption: the +0x18/+0x10 links form a tree: each node is reached exactly once; the routine keeps no visited set, so shared nodes would be destroyed twice
traversal.order: post-order over the whole structure: for each node in the +0x10 chain starting at the root, destroy its +0x18 subtree first, then tear the node down, then move to the next +0x10 node
traversal.unrolling_note: the compiler unrolled the first levels of the +0x18 descent inline (the descent blocks chain through registers before the single self-recursive call); the observable free order is the post-order above regardless of unrolling
